items.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000
items.q: So we went out and talked to him and said, “Geez I sure would like to see that band. He said, “Well,” he says, “I’ll tell you what, meet me here at intermission and I’ll take you in.”

ctx.x: No. My father became so. He caught the bug. He caught the bug really during the war when he was playing my stuff he thought that’s not bad you know. And I was really hooked on it. I’ll tell you one story that remains bright in my mind. A friend of mine and I were in Washington, DC at my grandmother’s house and I think it was ’35 or ‘6, when the Spanish Civil War was going on, whenever the hell that was. And the Benny Goodman band was to play at the Raleigh Hotel in downtown Washington. And we decided we had to…

That’s amazing. It’s so interesting, because I think back when I was that age, and I was a bit older, but the Beatles came in, and there was all that flak about them and that hype, and the girls loved them. And now I look at my own kids, and they have their own little stars. But the swing guys were your stars.
